data.text:
At least five people died in Vietnam after Typhoon Kalmaegi pummelled coastal regions with destructive winds and heavy rain, officials said on Friday, Nov. 7, following the storm's deadly passage through the Philippines where it killed at least 188 people.

The typhoon made landfall in central Vietnam late on Thursday, Nov. 6, uprooting trees, damaging homes, and triggering power outages, before weakening as it moved inland.

In Gia Lai province where Kalmaegi directly made landfall, people were seen gathering at places with a power generator to charge their mobile phones, while in another community, villagers brought containers to carry clean water home from a small waterfall nearby.

Vietnam's disaster management agency reported seven injuries and damage to approximately 2,800 homes after Typhoon Kalmaegi left Vietnam. Large scale power outages also affected about 1.3 million people, it said.

Authorities have warned of more heavy rainfall in central provinces and said rising river levels from Hue to Dak Lak could trigger flooding and landslides.

Courtesy: Reuters

'PLEASE STOP STEALING': KAREN DAVILA SLAMS CORRUPTION AMID CEBU FLOODS THAT KILLED 188

Broadcast journalist Karen Davila condemned systemic corruption in government projects after severe flooding in Cebu left at least 188 people dead—the worst flash flood in the province's history.

In a post on X (formerly Twitter) on Friday, November 7, Davila questioned how such devastation could occur despite Cebu having 414 flood control projects worth ₱26.7 billion from 2022 to 2025.

"HOW CORRUPTION MAY HAVE COST LIVES. 188 dead and rising. The worst flash flood in the history of the province. Cebu has 414 flood control projects worth to P26.7 billion from 2022 to 2025 - meant to protect our people, homes and livestock. What happened?!" she wrote, adding that widespread flooding across the Philippines happens because "the funds for flood control are being stolen."

Davila lamented that while extreme weather conditions continue to worsen, "systemic corruption" aggravates the suffering of ordinary Filipinos.

"Nakaka-awa ang ordinaryong Pilipino. Habang nagdurusa sa hirap at kalamidad, maraming pulitiko naliligo sa nakaw na yaman. PLEASE. STOP. STEALING," she said.

data.text:
The latest update on Typhoon #UwanPH. 
Please take note of the sheer size of this storm. It has just entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility and it's already producing Signal 1 & 2 wind conditions **well outside** even the orange circular area that customarily denotes where you find sustained tropical storm strength winds. If you know anyone not taking this storm seriously, please encourage them to do so. I don't typically get alarmist about typhoons because they're a fact of life in the Philippines, but this storm is a *life threatening event* that will have broad impacts across Luzon and potentially catastrophic impacts where the eye of the storm makes landfall if predictions that it will hit Luzon as a Super Typhoon hold true. So far, they are doing just that, but the storm has developed a bit more slowly than predicted. 
If you know people living in low lying areas, near running water (particularly on river bends and flood plains) or in areas with any history of flooding, mountain valleys or landslide susceptible zones, encourage them to evacuate by Sunday early afternoon at the latest. It could save their lives. 
This storm will have wide ranging impacts and disruptive consequences. Torrential rain and sustained gale force winds will impact much of Luzon, with areas within or adjacent to the eye wall being worst. Power and communications will likely be lost for wide areas across Luzon. Payment systems that rely on internet connectivity are likely to be disrupted. Be prepared to be self-sufficient for 3-5 days. Have food, water, gas for generators, and batteries fully charged. Know where your family and friends are located physically during the storm. Have plans to link up with them and check on their safety. Have cash. Secure your belongings and protect them with plastic sheeting if they may be vulnerable to wind and water damage in your home. Move furniture to higher levels of the home if you live in a flood prone area. Move vehicles to shelter on higher ground (not under trees). These are just some basic preparedness tips that can help mitigate the impact of this storm on you and your family. Stay safe Pilipinas 🇵🇭
